text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak, in its instructions to newly appointed governors, said they had to get out of their offices to the field and take an interest in the problems of the masses. Fourteen provincial governors took the oath of office yesterday.
- Egypt and Tunisia say it is important to set up an Arab common market. An Egyptian-Tunisian coordination committee discussed promoting bilateral relations.
- Mubarak issued a decree appointing 14 ambassadors and 33 ministers plenipotentiary.
- Speaker of Parliament Fathi Sorour told members of the U.S. Congress that there is no persecution of Christians in Egypt and no restrictions on freedom of expression.
- Health Minister Ismail Sallam said the government would not hesitate to ban imports of meat from any state where the meat is proved not to be safe.
- New governors took the oath of office and had a meeting with President Mubarak.
- Mubarak said Egypt would help set up Beirut Islamic University.

- Health Minister Ismail Sallam said his ministry had appealed against a court ruling which overturned a ministerial ban on female circumcision. He said he would not allow the operation to take place in hospitals.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said it would be decided whether there was a need for a minister for the Toshka project in the light of the performance of the ministries of agriculture and irrigation and the local province and the level of coordination between them.

- A criminal court will give its verdict in the case of Abdelwahhab el-Habbak on Monday. Habbak faces charges of embezzling millions of dollars while chairman of the state's holding company for engineering industries.
- New assistant interior ministers start work.
- Newt Gingrich told Fathi Sorour that he never imagined reducing the level of U.S. aid to Egypt. He said Cairo was playing an important part in the peace process.
- A fire gutted the office of newly appointed Public Works and Water Resources Minister Mahmoud Abu Zaid.
